changelog.change: Initial entry — the nine high-yield interaction pairs plus antibiotic-specific idiosyncratic toxicity (fluoroquinolones, linezolid, daptomycin) and a QT-prolonging drug-class quick list.

summary: Nine interaction pairs that are easy to miss because neither drug is obviously dangerous alone — mechanism, the actual risk, and the bedside fix for each. Plus three antibiotic toxicities that surface after the patient has already left the visit where the prescription was written.

rows: Methotrexate + NSAIDs
NSAIDs reduce renal tubular secretion of methotrexate, raising serum levels.
Risk scales with MTX dose — high-dose oncologic regimens are most dangerous. Caution even at low rheumatologic doses; avoid unsupervised OTC NSAID use.
Digoxin + Amiodarone
Amiodarone inhibits P-glycoprotein efflux and renal tubular clearance of digoxin.
PO digoxin levels rise ~70%, IV ~17%. Check level before starting amiodarone; reduce digoxin dose 30-50% (PO) or 15-30% (IV).
Azithromycin + QT-prolonging drugs
Additive QT prolongation with other QT-prolonging agents.
Check baseline QTc before adding; avoid stacking a second QT-prolonging agent in at-risk patients (hypokalaemia, structural heart disease).
ACE inhibitors + Spironolactone
Both retain potassium via independent mechanisms — reduced aldosterone signalling plus direct aldosterone antagonism.
In CKD or HF, hyperkalaemia can stop the heart. Check potassium at 1-2 weeks after starting, and again thereafter — not a one-time check.
Ciprofloxacin + Warfarin
Ciprofloxacin inhibits CYP1A2, which clears R-warfarin, causing unpredictable INR elevation.
Check INR early after starting, adjust as needed. Nitrofurantoin is a safer UTI alternative in a warfarin patient when clinically appropriate.
Linezolid + SSRIs
Linezolid is a reversible MAO inhibitor; combined with an SSRI it raises serotonin syndrome risk.
Incidence is low but consequence is not. Check the medication list before starting linezolid in any patient on an SSRI or SNRI.
Clopidogrel + Omeprazole
Omeprazole inhibits CYP2C19, the enzyme required to convert clopidogrel to its active antiplatelet metabolite.
Reduces the active metabolite by ~46% and platelet inhibition by ~30-47%. Dosing 12 h apart does NOT fix this — the inhibition isn't timing-dependent. Use pantoprazole instead.
SSRIs + Tramadol
Both raise synaptic serotonin — SSRI via reuptake inhibition, tramadol via reuptake inhibition plus weak mu-opioid activity.
Additive serotonergic effect (serotonin syndrome risk), plus tramadol independently lowers seizure threshold. Use caution combining with any serotonergic therapy.
Statins + Clarithromycin
Clarithromycin inhibits CYP3A4, the primary metabolic pathway for simvastatin and lovastatin, raising statin levels.
Rhabdomyolysis risk with simvastatin/lovastatin plus a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. Hold the statin during the antibiotic course, or switch to pravastatin/rosuvastatin (not CYP3A4-dependent).

body.text: Antibiotic toxicity — the other side of stewardship
Several antibiotics carry dose-independent or idiosyncratic toxicity that's easy to miss because it develops after the patient has already left the visit where the prescription was written.

rows: Fluoroquinolones
Tendinopathy and rupture

Direct toxic effect on tendon fibroblasts. Achilles tendinopathy OR 4.3, rupture OR 2.0 vs non-users (UK database, 6.4M patients). Amplified by age > 60, concurrent corticosteroids, renal transplant. Onset hours to weeks (average 6-10 days) and can occur after stopping. Stop the drug and rest the tendon at first symptom.
Linezolid
Peripheral neuropathy

Mitochondrial protein-synthesis inhibition impairs Schwann-cell function with prolonged exposure. Strongly duration-dependent (typically after weeks). Numbness/pain concentrate in the feet; may be only partially reversible. Avoid courses beyond 28 days when possible.
Daptomycin
Myopathy

A membrane-level effect on myocytes parallels its antibacterial mechanism. Concurrent statin therapy compounds the risk — consider holding the statin during the course. Baseline CK, then weekly during therapy; discontinue if CK rises significantly with myalgia, or exceeds roughly 10× ULN regardless of symptoms.

items: Antimicrobials: macrolides (azithromycin, erythromycin), fluoroquinolones, antifungal azoles
Antiarrhythmics: amiodarone, sotalol, dofetilide, procainamide, quinidine
Other: methadone, certain antidepressants (citalopram at higher doses)

body.text: Stacking two or more agents from this list multiplies risk beyond any single agent's individual QTc effect — reconcile the FULL medication list, not just the newest addition, before prescribing any QT-prolonging antimicrobial.
